_comment: Recorded coaching transcripts used to check the summariser prompt. Add a case by appending an object here — no code change needed. Names are invented; nothing here is a real athlete. Keep transcripts realistic: run-on sentences, filler and Whisper mishearings are the point, because that is what the model actually receives.

cases.why: The case Team Talk exists for: one squad talk naming two athletes, saved once per member.
cases.transcript: Right, good session everyone. Ana, your first step is still late, you're waiting for the ball instead of reading the setter. Jonas, that was the best you've blocked all year, genuinely. And everybody, the back row is silent out there, I want to hear you calling. Next week we're going to work on serve receive.

cases.why: The ordinary one-to-one recording where the coach never says the name. Must produce the pre-personalisation prompt exactly.
cases.transcript: Okay so today was decent, the platform is holding up much better under pressure but you're still dropping your elbow on the follow through. Work on keeping it locked. Next session let's do twenty minutes on that.

cases.why: Anastasia is on the roster and Ana is not mentioned. A naive word-boundary test personalises Ana's summary off Anastasia's name.
cases.transcript: Anastasia was excellent in the middle today, really quick off the mark, and the rest of you need to match that energy.

cases.why: ASCII word boundaries do not work on non-ASCII letters. Zoe must not match Zoë, and Zoë must match itself.
cases.transcript: Zoë covered the tip really well in the second half, that is exactly the read I want to see.

cases.why: Sport is resolved server-side and can still come back null. The prompt must take the general branch rather than guessing a sport.
cases.transcript: Good work today, much better tempo than last week, keep the intensity up.

cases.why: Whisper output from a noisy sports hall. The prompt must still be well formed; the model is instructed to bail rather than invent.
cases.transcript: uh so yeah the the thing with the with the sat was was not not great um libro

cases.why: A squad with two Jacks. The coach corrects one of them by name; the transcript cannot say which. A first name is not an identifier, so neither Jack may be told their coach said this about them — the generic summary is the only honest output.
cases.transcript: Right, listen in. Jack, you're dropping your elbow on contact and that's why you're losing the ball. Priya, your clearing was sharp today, keep that. Everyone else, ruck speed was better than Tuesday.

cases.why: Will is on the roster and is never addressed. 'you will need to' is a coach saying an auxiliary verb. Case-insensitive matching turned that into a personalised summary for a child who was not spoken to.
cases.transcript: Good set. You will need to get your hands up earlier on the catch, all of you, and we're going to do more of that next week with more grace through the stroke.

cases.why: The other half of the rule. Will IS addressed here, capitalised, as a coach addressing a person. Requiring the capital must not cost a real personalisation.
cases.transcript: Will, hands up earlier on the catch. Grace, your turns were the best in the lane today.

replies.content:
• Read the setter instead of waiting for the ball.
• The back row is silent — call for it.
NEXT: Read the setter early on serve receive.

expect.next: Read the setter early on serve receive.

replies.content:
• Platform is holding up under pressure.
• Elbow is dropping on the follow through.

replies.why: A NEXT line over the limit is the model writing prose. It is dropped rather than shown to a child as an instruction.
replies.content:
• Good session.
NEXT: Work on keeping the elbow locked through the follow through and also read the setter earlier and call louder in the back row and keep your feet moving throughout.

replies.why: The prompt forbids 'NEXT: none' but models do it anyway.
The instructed output for a transcript too garbled to summarise.

splits._comment: One recording about several athletes, split into one summary each (lib/split-summary.ts). `cases` hold the name gate that decides who the model may write for at all; `replies` are recorded model replies, parsed against `requested`. Add either by appending — no code change needed.

cases.why: The shape Max asked for: talk about two athletes by name in one breath. Leo was chosen but never spoken to, so the model must never be asked to write for him.
cases.transcript: Okay so quick one on the two of you. Kai, your approach was rushed again, you're jumping off two feet too early, slow the last two steps down. Mia, really good tempo on the quick set today, keep your hands high. Both of you, call the ball earlier, I want to hear it. Next time Kai we're doing approach footwork first thing.

cases.why: Two athletes called Sam in one recording. 'Sam, your arm swing' cannot be attributed, so neither Sam is written for and both are told why.
cases.transcript: Sam, your arm swing is dropping at the end. Priya, lovely footwork, keep that. Sam you need to stay lower on defence.

replies.why: Both athletes, each with their own points.
replies.content: {"athletes": [{"id": "a-kai", "summary": "\u2022 Slow the last two steps of your approach.\n\u2022 Call the ball earlier.", "next": "Approach footwork first thing."}, {"id": "a-mia", "summary": "\u2022 Good tempo on the quick set \u2014 keep your hands high.\n\u2022 Call the ball earlier.", "next": ""}]}

replies.why: The model left Mia out. She still gets a section — an empty one, said to be empty — never someone else's.
replies.content: {"athletes": [{"id": "a-kai", "summary": "\u2022 Slow the last two steps of your approach.", "next": ""}]}

replies.why: A section for an id nobody asked for — a hallucinated athlete, and Leo, who was chosen but not named — is dropped whatever it says.
replies.content: {"athletes": [{"id": "a-kai", "summary": "\u2022 Slow the last two steps.", "next": ""}, {"id": "a-stranger", "summary": "\u2022 STRANGER-TEXT must never surface.", "next": "STRANGER-NEXT"}, {"id": "a-leo", "summary": "\u2022 LEO-TEXT must never surface.", "next": ""}, {"id": "a-mia", "summary": "\u2022 Keep your hands high.", "next": ""}]}

replies.why: Kai's section names Mia. The prompt forbids it; the parser withholds it rather than showing Kai a sentence about Mia.
replies.content: {"athletes": [{"id": "a-kai", "summary": "\u2022 Slow your approach, like Mia does.", "next": ""}, {"id": "a-mia", "summary": "\u2022 Keep your hands high.", "next": ""}]}

replies.why: A code fence around the JSON is tolerated; a 'None' placeholder is nothing, not a summary; an over-long next is dropped.
Prose instead of JSON. Reported as an error to the coach, never guessed at.
